summary: A Blender-authored stone guildhall exported as a 661 KB GLB: plinth, string course, capped chimney, a twelve-course tiled gable roof, twelve windows glazed 20 cm inside 42 cm walls, four material slots and four sockets carried in glTF node extras.
objective: Drop a hero building into a village scene as a single loadAsync call and still get the kit contract back: a group at ground level, named sockets read from the asset itself, and a detail ladder that survives from thirty metres to arm's length.
intent_signals: load a blender building into three js
glb hero building for a village
example_prompts: Put a stone guildhall at the head of the village square.
I need a GLB hero building I can attach a banner and a chimney to.
not_for: A measured reconstruction of any real guildhall, guild practice or period construction.
Assets that must stay editable as a .blend; this one is regenerated from the export script, not from a saved file.
Draco-compressed delivery: the GLB is uncompressed on purpose so the offline harness can read it without a decoder.

silhouette: gable block 8.0 m wide and 6.57 m deep with the ridge at 7.30 m, roughly twice the height of the timber cottage it stands beside
40 degree tiled roof with a 34 cm eave overhang and a capped ridge, broken at 2.2 m off centre by a stone chimney whose cap tops out at 8.17 m
stone plinth 35 cm proud of the wall face and an entrance step standing 70 cm outside the front wall
medium: twelve openings cut clean through 42 cm walls: two upper and two lower windows on each front and back wall, three per gable-end wall, plus the door
glazing set back 20 cm from the outer face so every reveal is a shadowed recess rather than a flat panel
string course ledge at 3.02 m dividing the wall into two storeys, a recessed timber door leaf 16 cm inside its opening, and twelve roof courses each lapping 10 cm over the one below
fine: 2 cm single-segment chamfer on every stone arris, applied by a bevel modifier limited to 35 degrees and baked in by export_apply
mullion and transom bars 5 cm square crossing each window 15 cm inside the reveal
four named material slots with distinct roughness (stone 0.88, tile 0.74, timber 0.62, glazing 0.12) so the surfaces separate under one light

principles: A glTF hero is still a kit part. It has to return the same { group, sockets, colliders } shape as a procedural module, or every consumer needs a special case for it.

Sockets belong in the asset, not in a table beside it. Blender empties carrying custom properties survive the export as node extras, so the attachment points cannot drift away from the geometry they were authored against.
Wall thickness is what makes stone read as stone: an opening cut flush with the face looks like a decal at every distance, and no material can rescue it.
implementation: Load it through the thin wrapper templates/kits/gltf/stone-guildhall.js: `const { group, sockets } = await create({ scale: 1 });`. The wrapper's create returns a Promise rather than a value -- the only place in the kit library where that is true -- because the geometry lives in a file.
The wrapper reads sockets from object.userData, which GLTFLoader fills from the node extras; the record's socket list is the same data written down, not a second source of truth.

Exporter keywords, verified present on Blender 5.2.1 LTS (111 operator properties): export_format='GLB', export_apply=True, export_yup=True, export_extras=True, export_lights=False, export_draco_mesh_compression_enable=False, export_animation_mode='ACTIONS', export_force_sampling=True.
export_apply=True bakes the bevel modifier into the exported mesh, so the chamfers are real geometry in the GLB and nothing has to be re-applied at load time.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible in the frame.

Parse the GLB JSON chunk: four named materials, one mesh with four primitives, POSITION/NORMAL/TEXCOORD_0 on each, and four nodes whose extras carry a socket name and a three-component normal (examples/early-slice/kits-gltf.test.js does exactly this).
KHR_draco_mesh_compression must not appear in extensionsUsed, and extensionsRequired must be absent, or the offline harness cannot decode the file.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here measures any real building, stone, joinery or guild.

The mesh is built in bpy from the parameters in export-village-assets.py rather than opened from a .blend, so no binary source is committed and the asset is reproducible from the script; the consequence is that the shape can only be changed by editing Python, not by modelling.

The poly budget is the triangle count of the exported mesh (8908 triangles, 19328 vertices) at the authored parameters. There are no LODs: the same 8908 triangles are drawn at the far view as at the detail view.

661 KB uncompressed -- almost all of it float32 position, normal and UV data for 19328 vertices. That is inside the 2 MB validator cap but two orders of magnitude above a procedural module, and Draco is deliberately off, so a bandwidth-sensitive delivery needs its own compressed copy.
The 8 m x 6.57 m footprint is the roof, chimney and step extent, not the wall line (7.2 m x 5.4 m); plots planned on the wall line will overlap the eaves.
Blender 5.2.1 LTS keyword presence was checked with bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf.get_rna_type().properties; no comparison was made against the 4.5 documentation the source record was written from.

T2 is not available for this blueprint: a gltf-asset record is loaded as its .glb by the harness and by every consumer, so buildKit's runtime surface and occlusion pass (see knowledge.surface-tier-defaults) never runs on it.
creative_affordances: Scale is a free parameter: the record proves 1.0, but the same GLB reads as a town hall at 1.4 and as a chapel at 0.8.
Swap the four materials after loading -- they are named, so group.traverse and a name switch is enough to move the building between the listed looks or to an unlisted one.
Attach a chimney, banner or hanging lantern through the named sockets rather than by hand-placing world coordinates.

defaults.rationale: Wall thickness and recess were chosen so the reveal still reads as a shadow at the close proof distance of about fourteen metres, where a 12 cm recess of the cottage scale would have closed up.

T0.note: Bevelled box from the proof log bounds: the eight-metre frontage and the ridge height.

T2.note: Tested, not assumed: with this tiers block in place, scripts/kit-proof.py --tier T2 wrote a proof log reading tier T1 and surface null. The GLB material base colours listed here are perfectly hex-keyable, but kit_proof_harness.tier_asset serves a gltf-asset record as the .glb itself and _harness/blueprint-views.loadBlueprint takes the GLTFLoader branch, which never calls buildKit; a wrapper create() returns a Promise, which buildKit cannot consume synchronously. So the families map is documentation of what T2 would use, not a tier this blueprint can show. Not proved, and no captures are claimed.

T3.note: The record's own asset is already a baked glTF, so T1 and T3 would be the same file; no second, higher bake ships.

T4.note: No external asset ships with this skill.
